newsitem.title: UK: London platinum, palladium fixed sharply higher.
newsitem.headline: London platinum, palladium fixed sharply higher.

text.p: Platinum fixed at $395.25 an ounce in London on Monday, the highest fix since February 28 and representing a rise of $12.25 from Friday afternoon.
The price of palladium fixed $7.25 higher at $171.75 an ounce, the highest level since April 20, 1995.
Both metals opened sharply higher in European trade on Monday following an equally strong rise on Friday, traders said.

Swiss-based traders said platinum surged on continued uncertainty about Russia's platinum group metals (PGM) delivery contracts with Japan. Delays since December have led to strong physical demand in the open market. The platinum market was thin and this exagerated the gains.

The dollar's sharp fall against the yen last week fuelled the precious metals complex from their listless and rangebound state. The dollar fell to below 118 yen -- the lowest level in nearly four months -- but then bounced slightly.

Platinum traded up to $396.50 an ounce, compared with its $386.00/$387.00 close on Friday and with the previous high this year of $398.75 on February 28. Palladium, a rare white metal used in electronics and auto catalysts, reached a session peak of $172.00 an ouce, a gain of $6.50. This compares with the fix on April 20, 1995 of $174.80.
Gold was at a one-month high of $348.30, up $2.35 from Friday's close. Silver stood a cent up at $4.87/$4.89.
